chapter_metadata.title: Balloon Dilation Techniques
key_points: Airway stenosis has multiple etiologies including iatrogenic, infectious, inflammatory, malignant, idiopathic, and traumatic causes.
Balloon dilation (balloon bronchoplasty) is a simple, safe, inexpensive, and rapidly effective technique for immediate airway improvement.
Direct bronchoscopy is the gold standard for diagnosis and therapeutic intervention.
Balloons should be long enough to straddle the stenosis with ≥1 cm overlap on both sides.
Balloon dilation may be repeated or combined with adjuncts (stenting, laser, cryotherapy, medications).
chapter_metadata.reference: Kovitz KL, Yong SS. Balloon Dilation Techniques. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_35-1

clinical_procedures.name: Balloon bronchoplasty
clinical_procedures.purpose: Immediate relief of central airway obstruction from stenosis
steps: Establish airway (laryngeal mask airway, ET tube, or rigid bronchoscope)
Pass balloon catheter through bronchoscope channel or over wire
Position balloon across stenosis with ≥1 cm overlap on both sides
Inflate to target diameter for ~1 min, repeat ×3
clinical_procedures.notes: Deep sedation/anesthesia typically required; avoid wire-only placement without visualization.

clinical_pearls: Balloon bronchoplasty is simple, safe, inexpensive, repeatable, and rapidly effective.
Superficial airway lacerations may paradoxically prolong airway patency (~24 months vs 4 months without laceration in TB-related stenosis).

points: Balloon bronchoplasty is a safe, quick, effective, and repeatable method for airway stenosis.
Symptomatic relief is immediate in most patients.
Can be stand-alone or bridge to stenting or surgery.
